paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning methods for Fourier-based distribution estimation with application in option pricing

summary: The paper proposes two PQC-based quantum machine learning approaches for option pricing that approximate the PDF or CDF of Black–Scholes asset distributions using Fourier series learned from 4–8 qubit circuits (4–8 layers) trained on datasets of 250–10,000 samples. Experiments are performed entirely in classical simulation using PennyLane, and results show convergence of estimated option prices for strikes K={90,100,110}. A QAMC baseline using amplitude estimation requires roughly 2000–7000 shots per Fourier coefficient (~5000 average) but is used only as a benchmarking reference rather than demonstrating computational advantage.

experiments.description: Method I: supervised-learning PQC to approximate the PDF of the underlying asset distribution, extract Fourier coefficients via DFT, and price a European vanilla put option under Black-Scholes dynamics.

algorithm.variant: supervised learning for PDF approximation with parametrized quantum circuits
algorithm.ansatz: 2-qubit layered ansatz with Rx(x) data encoding and Ry(θ) trainable rotations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input x is encoded through Rx(x) gates; trainable parameters are implemented with Ry(θ) rotations in a layered PQC.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize empirical H1 risk for PDF approximation: RS_h1(f*,f)= (1/I)Σ_i[(f*(xi)-f(xi))^2 + (df*/dx(xi)-df/dx(xi))^2]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond H1 differential loss; Fourier coefficients of payoff computed analytically

problem_instance.description: European vanilla put option pricing at t0=0 under Black-Scholes dynamics; PDF of normalized log-price is approximated and used to compute option value.

dataset_specification.description: S0=100, r=0.1, T=1, σ=0.25, strikes K in {90,100,110}; normalized log-price Xt=log(St/K) ~ N(log(S0/K)+(r-σ^2/2)t, σ^2 t)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prices transformed to normalized log-prices; data rescaled to [-π,π] and model trained in [-2π,2π] to reduce Gibbs phenomena
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 repetitions; convergence assessed versus exact option price across increasing dataset sizes and circuit dimensions

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: DFT applied to direct evaluations of the trained circuit; payoff Fourier coefficients computed analytically
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price computed from product of learned PDF Fourier coefficients and analytically derived payoff coefficients

speedup_claims.factor: competitive alternative; no explicit speedup factor reported
speedup_claims.conditions: for Fourier-coefficient extraction and option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports qualitative competitiveness and cost/accuracy comparison, but no asymptotic or numerical speedup factor for Method I.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed. Experiments use 6–8 qubits and 6–8 layers on a classical simulator with datasets up to 2.5×10^3 points.
limiting_factors: No asymptotic complexity comparison against classical Monte Carlo
All experiments performed on classical simulation
Training overhead of variational circuits not quantified

experiments.description: Method II: self-supervised-learning PQC to approximate the CDF from unlabeled samples, extract Fourier coefficients via DFT, and price a European vanilla put option under Black-Scholes dynamics.

algorithm.variant: self-supervised learning for CDF approximation with differential machine learning loss
algorithm.ansatz: 2-qubit layered ansatz with Rx(x) data encoding and Ry(θ) trainable rotations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input x is encoded through Rx(x) gates; trainable parameters are implemented with Ry(θ) rotations in a layered PQC.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize combined empirical risk for CDF and PDF terms: RX_T,l2,l2(F)= (1/I)Σ_i(F_emp*(xi)-F(xi))^2 - (2/I)Σ_i f(xi) + Q(f^2) plus endpoint constraints
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Endpoint constraints added to enforce CDF behavior at domain extremes; differential term uses PDF derivative information; Fourier coefficients of payoff computed analytically

problem_instance.description: European vanilla put option pricing at t0=0 under Black-Scholes dynamics; CDF of normalized log-price is approximated from samples only.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Samples rescaled to [-π,π] and model trained in [-2π,2π] to reduce Gibbs phenomena; empirical CDF used as pseudo-labels
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 repetitions; convergence assessed versus exact option price across increasing dataset sizes and circuit dimensions

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Empirical CDF construction from samples; DFT applied to direct evaluations of the trained circuit to recover exponential-series coefficients
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price computed from learned CDF Fourier coefficients and analytically derived payoff coefficients

limiting_factors: Training cost of PQCs not compared to classical density estimation

experiments.description: Method III: QAMC benchmark using modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (mRQAE) to estimate Fourier coefficients of the PDF and price the same European vanilla put option.

algorithm.variant: QAMC with modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (mRQAE)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: precision/tolerance set by mRQAE; increasing tolerance corresponds to fewer shots

hyperparameters.shots_per_coefficient: approximately 5000 on average for high accuracy

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Expectation value encoded into amplitudes of a quantum state for Monte Carlo-style integration; Fourier coefficients estimated from sampled paths
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Fourier coefficients Af_k and Bf_k of the PDF via amplitude estimation on sampled path states
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: mRQAE used to recover sign of coefficients; exact simulation assumed for asset evolution

problem_instance.description: Benchmark pricing of a European vanilla put option under Black-Scholes dynamics using Fourier coefficients of the PDF estimated by QAMC.

dataset_specification.description: S0=100, r=0.1, T=1, σ=0.25, strikes K in {90,100,110}; exact simulation of asset evolution assumed

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Direct sampling of simulated asset paths; coefficients estimated from sampled values of f(S_i) times sine/cosine basis functions
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Convergence evaluated by varying number of shots/tolerance; compared against Methods I and II in terms of cost and accuracy

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical estimation of Fourier coefficients from sampled paths; exact payoff coefficients computed analytically
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price computed from Fourier coefficient products

speedup_claims.factor: requires hundreds of thousands of shots for high accuracy
speedup_claims.baseline_method: Methods I and II / PQC-based approaches
speedup_claims.conditions: for high-accuracy option pricing with mRQAE and Fourier-coefficient estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a cost comparison in terms of shots, not a proven asymptotic speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Amplitude estimation requires thousands of circuit executions (~2000–7000 shots per coefficient). For realistic problems this would scale to hundreds of thousands of shots.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup of amplitude estimation vulnerable to constant-factor overhead
